subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should `openclaw models auth login` on non-loopback remote node hosts fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw support forwarding the resulting credentials to the gateway?
rationale: Both choices change where sensitive provider OAuth material may be acquired and persisted, so automation should not decide this credential boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with a clear instruction to run the command on the gateway host, while preserving local loopback and tunnel setups.

options.title: Design gateway credential forwarding
options.body: Add an authenticated gateway-side credential transfer/session flow so node-host login can safely update the gateway-owned auth store.

options.title: Warn but allow local write
options.body: Keep the existing permissive behavior with a warning, accepting that users can still consume credentials into the wrong store.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with a clear instruction to run the command on the gateway host, while preserving local loopback and tunnel setups.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent already authored the maintainer repair direction and verification for the exact remote-node auth guard.
